purpose: Implement catalog-only character 2-4 gram TF-IDF and test all 16 retrieval combinations.
hypothesis: n-gram retrieval may complement the existing string, phonetic and specification candidate channels.
changed_factors: S/N/P/T retrieval channel subset; resulting negative candidate pool
fixed_conditions: Original train order, splits and LightGBM parameters
Catalog-only TF-IDF fit; train-fold category and alias assets
Train-only positive injection; original hard-negative sampling

preprocessing.ngram_fit: official catalog only; char 2-4 TF-IDF on compact Unidecode names
preprocessing.shared_feature_cache: same public row and candidate independent of other query rows; fold-specific category features

training_pairs.negative_rule: subset candidates; if >100, top80 original hardness union top20 tonnage plus positive
training_pairs.language_weight: .7/p_H or .3/p_N on deduplicated train, applied per pair

metrics.metric_source: two overlapping public-train development splits; details in variants

cost.shared_cache: cache.*: all-path retrieval and union features, not per-combination end-to-end cost
cost.timing_scope: cached evaluation excludes retrieval/features; two experiments concurrently share CPU

observations: All 16 subsets completed; 15 separate models and one no-fit fixed-ID baseline.
SPT reproduces prior training-pair hash, holdout candidate hashes and all production predictions.
All 15 trained variants passed runtime/cached consistency and row-independence probes on both holdouts.
limitations: Development splits overlap and have already been inspected
Channel budgets fixed per path, union candidate counts vary
Search removal does not remove the corresponding reranking features
Two concurrently running processes shared a 2-CPU quota; per-variant training/cached timings must not be interpreted as deployment latency.
16 combinations were selected on observed development holdouts; potential selection bias and vessel-repeat dependence remain.
decision: SNPT selected by pre-recorded two-split mean vessel score; both unrestricted and N-enabled best. See reports/retrieval_combinations.json.

design.S: legacy normalized string retrieval: non-Hangul top24; Hangul uses P instead
design.N: romanized compact catalog names, char 2-4 TF-IDF, positive cosine top60 Hangul/top24 non-Hangul
design.P: legacy Hangul roman top60 + consonant key top60; extra phonetic key top24 for every language
design.T: legacy two-tonnage nearest and Hangul likely-type subsets
design.primary: pure retrieval: no call lookup or aliases
design.secondary: production lookup and fixed training-fold aliases enabled
design.empty: no retrieval; deterministic first catalog ID, no classifier training
design.selection: report unrestricted best and best N-enabled by mean vessel weighted accuracy, mixed production weighted accuracy, then fewer candidates. Package best N-enabled to implement requested n-gram.

fit.reason: No search: fixed first-catalog-ID baseline, with optional production lookup/alias handling.
